**Image 1: Projects Page (مشاريعنا)**

**(a) Are the project images visible and well-placed?**
Yes, the project images are clearly visible and well-positioned. The page uses an effective **alternating layout** (image-left/text-right, then text-left/image-right) that creates visual rhythm and prevents monotony. The solar panel installation photos are high-quality, properly cropped, and fill their containers appropriately without awkward stretching or cropping of key details.

**(b) Is the text readable over the images?**
Excellent readability. The design employs a **smart text placement strategy**: instead of placing text directly over busy image areas, the content is positioned on the **solid dark background overlay** at the bottom portion of each image section (or in dedicated white space beside the image). The white Arabic text contrasts sharply against the dark gradient, and the font size is generous. Even the "409.2 كيلووات" badge uses a light background with dark text for maximum legibility.

**(c) Does it look professional?**
Highly professional. This layout demonstrates enterprise-level UI/UX design with:
- Clean grid system with consistent spacing
- Sophisticated alternating pattern that guides the eye naturally
- Professional photography showcasing actual installations
- Clear information hierarchy (title → location/type → description → capacity metric)
- Cohesive color scheme (green accents matching the brand)
- Polished typography with proper Arabic text alignment

---

**Image 2: Home Page Projects Section**

**(a) Are the project images visible and well-placed?**
Yes, the three project cards feature prominent, high-quality installation photos as full-bleed backgrounds. The images are well-composed—showing battery storage systems and solar panel arrays—and are appropriately sized within the card grid. However, the layout is more compact than Image 1, with two cards on top and one below, which creates slight visual imbalance but remains functional.

**(b) Is the text readable over the images?**
Good readability with minor caveats. The text is placed over **darkened image overlays** (gradient masks), which provides sufficient contrast for the white headings and body text to be legible. The location badges ("مكة", "الرياض") use semi-transparent pill-shaped backgrounds that help them stand out. That said, because the text sits *directly* atop complex photographic details (wires, metal frames), it requires slightly more cognitive effort to read compared to Image 1's cleaner separation.

**(c) Does it look professional?**
Professional and conversion-focused. The card-based design works well for a homepage summary section:
- Modern card UI with rounded corners and subtle shadows
- Real project photos build trust and credibility
- Capacity metrics displayed prominently in floating badges (316.8, 409.2, 28.4 kW)
- Consistent internal card structure across all three projects
- The "Get Quote" CTA button in the header maintains brand consistency

---

### **Comparative Summary**
| Aspect | Image 1 (Projects Page) | Image 2 (Home Section) |
|--------|-------------------------|------------------------|
| **Layout** | Superior alternating layout with breathing room | Compact grid cards |
| **Text Clarity** | Excellent (text on solid zones) | Good (text on darkened photos) |
| **Visual Impact** | Magazine-quality presentation | Effective thumbnail preview style |
| **Best For** | Detailed project showcase | Quick homepage overview |

**Verdict:** Both implementations successfully use real project photography to establish credibility. **Image 1 represents the gold standard** for a dedicated projects gallery with its sophisticated alternating layout and superior text-image separation, while **Image 2 performs excellently as a condensed homepage teaser** that encourages users to click through to the full projects page.
